claims.claim_text: Avoid drinking coffee on an empty stomach to prevent acidity.

claim_origin.quote: Avoid drinking coffee on an empty stomach to prevent acidity.
Avoid drinking coffee on an empty stomach to prevent acidity.

claims.summary: In the two appraised abstracts, a review reports coffee-related gastric acid secretion and reflux, while a small before-and-after study measures sucrose permeability. Neither abstract establishes that avoiding coffee specifically on an empty stomach prevents a defined acid-related clinical outcome. This is an assisted, abstract-only assessment of a bounded selection, not a finding that coffee has no physiological effects or that the claim is false.
evidence_gaps: Define the intended acidity endpoint without treating acid secretion, reflux, heartburn and dyspepsia as interchangeable.
A controlled comparison of fasting coffee with an appropriate alternative, measuring the intended preventive outcome, is not reported in the appraised abstracts.
Contemporary evidence, population applicability, dose and coffee preparation, clinical importance, and study-level risk of bias have not been systematically assessed.
Assisted appraisal of 2/3 candidate abstracts. Other candidates were not appraised in this assessment. No full-text, exhaustive-search or systematic risk-of-bias appraisal was performed.

claims.claim_text: Eat fruits before meals, not after, for better digestion.

claim_origin.quote: Eat fruits before meals, not after, for better digestion.
Eat fruits before meals, not after, for better digestion.

claims.summary: The two appraised abstracts describe kiwifruit-related digestive benefits and baobab-extract experiments, but do not report a comparison of eating whole fruits before versus after meals on a defined human digestive outcome. This bounded assisted assessment cannot establish the timing recommendation or refute digestive benefits of particular fruits.
evidence_gaps: Better digestion is not a defined endpoint; digestive symptoms, transit, nutrient absorption and postprandial glycemia cannot be substituted silently.
A human whole-fruit before-versus-after-meal comparison with a defined digestive endpoint is not reported in the appraised abstracts.
Fruit species, dose, population, timing interval, clinical importance and generalizability require specification.
Assisted appraisal of 2/70 candidate abstracts. Other candidates were not appraised in this assessment. No full-text, exhaustive-search or systematic risk-of-bias appraisal was performed.

claims.claim_text: Maintain proper posture while sitting to prevent back pain.

claim_origin.quote: Maintain proper posture while sitting to prevent back pain.
Maintain proper posture while sitting to prevent back pain.

claims.summary: The two appraised abstracts concern treatment in people already experiencing low back pain and mixed review-level evidence about physical exposure and causality. They do not establish that an isolated, defined proper sitting posture prevents back-pain onset or recurrence. This bounded assisted assessment does not establish that posture is irrelevant or ineffective.
evidence_gaps: Define the proposed sitting posture and intended prevention population, including whether onset or recurrence is the target.
An isolated sitting-posture intervention with incident or recurrent back-pain outcomes is not established by the appraised trial abstract.
Confounding, mixed interventions, review overlap, risk of bias, effect sizes and clinical importance require further appraisal.
Assisted appraisal of 2/77 candidate abstracts. Other candidates were not appraised in this assessment. No full-text, exhaustive-search or systematic risk-of-bias appraisal was performed.

Replace sugary drinks with herbal tea for a healthier alternative.

claims.reason: Healthier is an unspecified comparative outcome. The supplied OCR does not identify a health endpoint, tea ingredients, preparation or added sugar. Defining the claim as unsweetened tea reducing weight, glycemia or disease risk would introduce details not stated here.
